name: Depwire

hlido_opinion.headline: The most substantiated tool in this batch — a deterministic dependency graph served to AI coders over MCP, with real benchmarks and an unusually honest anti-RAG pitch.
hlido_opinion.body: Depwire is a context layer that sits between an AI coding assistant and a codebase: tree-sitter parses every file, graphology builds a symbol-level dependency graph, and 23 MCP tools let Claude, Cursor, Aider or any MCP client query exact facts instead of guessing from embeddings. The positioning is refreshingly precise — "this is not RAG", "Depwire is the GPS, your AI is the driver" — and it declines to claim it replaces the assistant. The public surface is materially better evidenced than most agent tooling we see: a benchmark table across eleven real projects in eleven languages (Hono, Excalidraw, FastAPI, ASP.NET Docs at 5,655 files, nlohmann/json, Spring PetClinic) with file/symbol counts and parse times, a shipped v1.8.2, a VSCode extension, a GitHub Action, a hosted cloud option, and stewardship of an open CC0 spec (DAT) drafted against a NIST concept paper. Feature depth is genuinely broad — what-if simulation, pre-action verification, security scanning with graph-aware severity, structural diff between commits, dead-code detection, multi-agent file claiming. The caveats are the ordinary ones for a young tool: every performance number (40% fewer tool calls, 56% fewer file reads, 100% deterministic accuracy) is vendor-supplied and untested by us; the licence is BSL 1.1 rather than open source until it converts to Apache-2.0 in February 2029; Pro features sit behind $9.99/month; and it appears to be a single-vendor project (ATEF ATAYA LLC). We did not run it. STEADY reflects an unusually well-evidenced public surface, not a measured performance claim.

tier_rationale: STEADY (79) — the strongest public surface in this wave: a shipped v1.8.2 with a real distribution footprint (npm, VSCode Marketplace, GitHub Action, cloud app), 23 documented MCP tools, and a benchmark table across eleven named real-world repositories in eleven languages, which is more falsifiable evidence than nearly any agent tool publishes. Held below VITAL because every efficiency and accuracy figure is vendor-supplied and unverified by us, the licence is BSL 1.1 (not open source until 2029), and we reviewed the public surface only.
what_it_does_well: Deterministic tree-sitter/AST approach with an explicit, well-argued case against embedding-based retrieval
23 MCP tools — genuinely agent-first, not a human product with an API bolted on
Benchmarks published against eleven named real projects with file counts, symbol counts and parse times
Broad, coherent feature set: impact analysis, what-if simulation, pre-action verification, security scan, structural diff, dead-code detection
Multiple real distribution channels shipped (npm, VSCode extension, GitHub Action, hosted cloud app)
Runs locally by default — code never leaves the machine, and the security scanner needs no API key
Stewards an open CC0 spec (DAT) for signing AI agent actions, drafted against a NIST concept paper
what_it_fails_at: Every headline metric (40% fewer tool calls, 56% fewer file reads, 100% accuracy) is vendor-supplied and unverified by Hlido
BSL 1.1 licence — not open source until it converts to Apache-2.0 in Feb 2029, which blocks some commercial adoption
Apparently a single-vendor, single-author project (ATEF ATAYA LLC) — bus-factor and continuity risk
No named customers, adoption numbers, or third-party validation on the public surface
Pro features and the cloud dashboard are paid ($9.99/month) with limited detail on what the free tier omits
Not tested hands-on — graph accuracy on a large mixed-language monorepo is exactly the claim that needs measuring
best_for: Developers using Claude Code, Cursor, Cline or Aider on a codebase large enough that context retrieval is the bottleneck
Teams doing risky refactors who want blast-radius analysis before an AI edits anything
Mixed-language monorepos where cross-language dependency edges are invisible to text search
Anyone who wants local-only code analysis with no cloud parsing
not_recommended_for: Organisations whose licence policy excludes BSL-1.1 dependencies
Buyers who need audited performance figures rather than vendor benchmarks
Small single-file projects where the dependency graph adds no signal
Teams needing vendor-scale support guarantees or an SLA

compared_to.note: Depwire's own site frames the two as complementary — internal codebase structure (Depwire) plus external library docs (Context7) — rather than competing.

evidence_urls.claim: 23 MCP tools exposed to AI assistants, with a documented tool-by-tool table
Deterministic tree-sitter AST parsing across 17 languages, not embedding-based retrieval
Benchmarks across eleven named real projects (Hono 352 files/6,245 symbols; ASP.NET Docs 5,655 files/42,827 symbols)
40% fewer tool calls / 56% fewer file reads / 100% deterministic accuracy
Shipped v1.8.2 under BSL 1.1, converting to Apache-2.0 on 2029-02-25
Steward of the CC0 Depwire Action Token (DAT) spec for signing AI agent actions

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: MCP-native by design: `npx -y depwire-cli mcp` exposes 23 tools to any MCP client, with a hosted endpoint via app.depwire.dev and a programmatic SDK at depwire-cli/sdk. This is a component other agents drive, not a destination product — the strongest agent-integration story in this wave.

checklist.evidence: 'Your AI doesn't know your architecture. Depwire does.'
Free CLI; Pro features $9.99/month; cloud app available
Benchmark table across 11 named real projects; no third-party validation

summary: The most substantiated tool in this batch — a deterministic dependency graph served to AI coders over MCP, with real benchmarks and an unusually honest anti-RAG pitch.
